title: Autoflow Runlet: Parameterized Runbooks as Safe, Observable Admin Tasks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: oncall and SREs repeatedly execute informal runbooks that are hard to parameterize, test, and audit. Current admin scripts live in repos and ad-hoc docs; this increases blast radius and slows remediation. Goal: introduce 'Autoflow Runlet' — a first-class, parameterized runbook artifact that can be executed as a guarded task via the Console and API with built-in dry-run, RBAC gating, input validation, telemetry, and automatic rollback/fallback policies.

Scope:
- A light manifest format for runlets (YAML/JSON as a string payload) that declares inputs, output assertions, required secrets, and idempotency hints.
- Execution API (/v1/admin/runlets/execute) that returns an execution id and supports dry-run, simulated side-effects, and replay.
- Console surface to list runlets, show required permissions, run history, and one-click dry-run vs execute.
- Telemetry hooks that emit structured events: runlet.started, runlet.step.completed, runlet.rollback.invoked, runlet.finished, plus token/latency cost for any steps that call inference endpoints.
- Safety controls: RBAC gating (define which roles can execute), execution quotas, two-step approval for destructive runlets, capability to pin a canary execution to a staging tenant.
- Audit logging integration with Private KMS-backed audit stream and retention policy.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Lightweight DSL vs full workflow engine: choose a constrained declarative runlet manifest (inputs, steps, assertions) to avoid the complexity of supporting arbitrary long-running state machines. Allows easier review and faster iteration.
- Steps are typed: CLI, HTTP, GH PR merge, infra API, service-annotated calls (e.g., call to /admin/evict-cache). Avoid embedding arbitrary scripts to keep VCS reviewability and provenance.
- Dry-run fidelity: dry-run will validate inputs and run step 'simulators' (no external side-effects) and run assertions. This reduces accidental changes but cannot fully guarantee parity. We'll document gaps and add step-level simulation factories over time.
- Telemetry attachment to runtime: instrument each step with token and latency cost if it invokes hosted inference or runtime APIs to make runlet cost-visible in the Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Create runlet manifest schema and publish Confluence design (link below).
- Implement execution API and storied execution metadata (start/finish/step outcomes).
- UI: Console runlet list, run modal with parameter form, dry-run toggle, and execution trace viewer.
- E2E tests covering RBAC gating, dry-run simulation, rollback path, and telemetry emission.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Autoflow+Runlets+Spec (draft)
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoflow-runlets (branch: feature/exec-api-proto)
- Draft Console UI mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X-RunletMocks (permission: redwood-internal)
- Dashboard: Grafana runlet-executions panel (shared dashboard id 1243)

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal SRE + core infra (opt-in) — runlets allowed only in staging tenants, require approval.
2) Beta: broader infra + firstline oncall teams, add quick templates (cache-evict, scale-up, restart-pod).
3) GA: enable in customer-managed Private deployments with RBAC fully enforced and audit retention.

Risks & mitigation:
- Accidental destructive actions: mitigate via approval flows and two-step confirmations plus tag 'destructive' in manifest.
- Incomplete dry-run parity: surface known gaps in UI and block runlets with high-risk steps unless force-enabled.
- Telemetry noise: sample non-critical runlets at 5% initially and tune.

Notes on integration with existing work:
- Reuses the admin task/shortflow patterns from ENG-271888 (taskify-maintenance-checklists-into-microflows) for compatibility with existing tooling.
- Observability and telemetry schema will align with ENG-314162 (ops-telemetry-curator-and-taskified-playbook-handoff) to avoid creating parallel event vocab.

Operational metrics to track:
- Mean time to remediation (MTTR) for incidents where a runlet was used vs previous baseline.
- Dry-run to execute conversion rate.
- Fraction of runlets with rollback invoked.
- Token and latency cost attributed to runlets per week.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finalize runlet schema and publish Confluence spec (owner: Marco Diaz).
- Implement execute API skeleton and persistence table for executions (owner: Marco).
- Add initial 3 runlet templates (cache-evict, restart-service, emergency-rollback) and internal docs.
- Coordinate with Security for RBAC/audit review (see comments).
